source.title: From Concepts to Components: Concept-Agnostic Attention Module Discovery in Transformers
source.authors: Jingtong Su; Julia Kempe; Karen Ullrich

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether suppressing a safety-related representation increases harmful compliance, using a contrastively discovered attention-head module and scalar intervention rather than the original single-direction projection.
record.gate_note: The safety vector is formed from harmful and harmless prompts, but the intervention scales a top-10 attention-head module, not one residual-stream direction projected out at every layer and position. The positive safety intervention is described as causing repetition, not as refusal of harmless requests, so it is not a refusal row. The GCG and ORTHO comparison results and the starred DR values are identified as taken from Arditi et al. and are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study takes Arditi et al.'s harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means vector as a tool to rank attention heads. It then scales 10 heads with its own method (SAMI) and reports only that method's HarmBench ASR against ORTHO and GCG baselines. It never ablates or adds the direction itself. It never tests whether one direction mediates refusal, nor whether jailbreaks act through it. The result is a method-performance figure, which makes this T4, not a test of V1 or V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors present SAMD/SAMI as a concept-agnostic attribution and intervention pipeline. They report that diminishing the 'safety' module jailbreaks models on HarmBench and claim it is more powerful than ORTHO and GCG. They also state they do not emphasize causality and that the module may be over- or incomplete.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a harmful-minus-harmless concept vector to rank attention heads, then scales a top-10 attention-head module with SAMI; it does not project a single residual-stream direction out of every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: The model-specific negative intervention strengths differ: s = -1.7 for Llama-2-Chat-7B, -0.7 for Qwen-Chat-7B, and -0.8 for Gemma-7B-IT.

fits_no_version.finding: Attention heads ranked by cosine similarity to the harmful-minus-harmless vector concentrate in middle layers (11-18 in Llama-2-chat-7B). Negatively scaling the top 10 heads raises HarmBench ASR to 71.1 (Llama-2-7B), 78.0 (Qwen-7B) and 84.3 (Gemma-7B-IT; DR 8.2). Positive scaling yields repetition of 'safety' tokens, not refusal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal can be largely removed by scaling a sparse set of about 10 attention heads whose outputs align with the refusal difference-in-means direction.

record.problems: The tested intervention targets a selected attention-head module, not the original single direction. The paper does not report uncertainty for the HarmBench ASRs or test whether other capabilities are preserved after safety-module intervention. Some comparison values in Table 2 are cited from Arditi et al., rather than results of this study.
record.rows_left_out: None due to the row limit. The starred DR, GCG, and ORTHO results in Table 2 are marked as taken from Arditi et al. and were not recorded as this study's results.

untested.parts: Ablating the difference-in-means direction, adding it to induce refusal, and capability retention after the safety intervention. The direction is used only to select heads.
Whether jailbreak attacks suppress the refusal direction, and training against ablation.
No abliterated released model is evaluated by the study, apart from the unclear-provenance ORTHO baseline.

missing.what: Unstarred Gemma-7B-IT ORTHO (weight orthogonalization) ASR of 73.0 and GCG ASR of 53.5, against DR 8.2. These appear to be this study's own baseline runs, and ORTHO on Gemma would bear on V1/V2 removal. Provenance is not stated explicitly.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is downgraded from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. The refusal direction serves only as a selection vector, and the reported numbers measure the study's own method. ASR values lack uncertainty, and no capability check accompanies the safety intervention.

versions.untested_parts: Does not ablate the single direction at every layer and position; does not test adding that direction on harmless requests; does not measure other abilities after the safety intervention.
No released-model abliteration weight edit is tested. The paper says SAMI is equivalent to modifying attention output projection matrices, but reports forward-pass interventions.
Tests the study's own negative intervention on a discovered safety module, not whether other jailbreak attacks suppress the original direction; does not test training against ablation.
Does not compare a single direction with an affine representation, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
Does not separate harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
The safety module is discovered separately for each model; transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models is not tested.
Does not test how refusal-training method or timing determines whether a removable direction exists.
No reasoning models are tested for refusal-direction behavior.

relation.reason: It is mainly tool use (DIM vector to rank heads), but the study's own ORTHO baseline on Gemma-7B-IT (73.0 ASR vs DR 8.2) is a result on V2. Treat it as a weak, incidental test that rests on one table cell.

tranche.reason: The SAMI results are T4-type, but Table 2 also reports an unstarred (so not cited, by the caption) ORTHO weight-orthogonalization HarmBench ASR for Gemma-7B-IT: 73.0 vs DR 8.2. That is the original's V2 method and measure, and Arditi et al. are not the source. So the study's own results bear on V2, and the record's line that it never ablates the direction is contradicted for Gemma. The test is weak and incidental: the text gives no setup (direction, layer) for this baseline.

source_check.notes: Missing row: Gemma-7B-IT ORTHO HarmBench ASR 73.0 (DR 8.2, GCG 53.5; Table 2, unstarred) should be added as a V2 row (likely observed/supports, near Arditi's 79.2 for Qwen) with a verdict. In Table 2 only the Llama/Qwen DR, GCG and ORTHO values are cited from Arditi. Figs 19-20 captions say the Qwen/Gemma safety modules are 5 heads, but Sec 4.3 says K=10 for all models. Judge and n are not stated.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Negative SAMI intervention on the discovered safety module in the three chat/instruct models
reader_labels.reason: HarmBench ASR rises substantially, but remains below complete refusal removal, and the intervention is on a head module rather than the claimed single direction (r1-r3).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The study's negative safety-module intervention on HarmBench standard behaviors
reader_labels.reason: Suppressing the discovered safety module functions as a jailbreak intervention, with reported ASRs of 71.1, 78.0, and 84.3 (r1-r3).
